clue.text: Precise individual tripping the light fantastic

definitions.text: Precise individual tripping the light fantastic

parts.words: Precise individual tripping the light fantastic
parts.note: tripping the light fantastic is an old phrase for dancing; a precise individual dancing places each foot exactly, one measured move at a time

explanation.surface: A fussy, exacting person taking to the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a style of dancing built from exact footwork, the kind a precise person would perform.

clue.text: Put sow with cow inside and see the growth!

indicators.note: inside places the word for cow within the word for sow

parts.note: to seed is to sow
to awe is to cow or intimidate

explanation.surface: A farmyard instruction to put a female pig with a cow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sow' and 'cow' look like farm animals but are verbs: SEED and AWE.
explanation.definitionFit: Marine algae are plants that grow in the sea.

clue.text: She has food in the house a terrific amount

indicators.note: in signals that the letters lie within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A woman at home eats a huge quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who consumes meals, one who dines.

clue.text: Contributes about a thousand and one according to rules

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for contributes goes around the other letters

parts.note: donates means contributes or gives
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone gives a large sum in line with regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rules' looks like a noun for regulations; it is a verb, governs.
explanation.definitionFit: Exercising control or power over others.

clue.text: Raising a public school's record

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising lifts the word upward so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: Eton is a famous English public (private fee-paying) school

explanation.surface: Fundraising for a school's archive.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton College is a famous fee-paying English school; Britain calls such schools public schools.
explanation.definitionFit: A written jotting is a record of something.

clue.text: Anger-anger about nasty trait

indicators.note: about places the first word around the letters that follow

parts.note: ire is anger

indicators.note: nasty suggests the word trait is messed up into a new form

explanation.surface: Someone is furious about a horrible characteristic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' rearranges TRAIT into RITAT, which 'about' places within IRE.
explanation.definitionFit: To provoke annoyance in someone, to vex them.

clue.text: Coloured novice

explanation.surface: A beginner who is painted.
explanation.definitionFit: The colour of grass, and also an informal word for inexperienced or naive.

clue.text: Give some pleasure to tot in depression

indicators.note: in puts the word for tot inside the word for depression

parts.note: a glen is a valley, a depression in the land
to tot up is to add

explanation.surface: Cheer up a small child who is feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' and 'depression' look like a sad child; they mean ADD and GLEN, a Scottish valley.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone happy or delighted.

clue.text: Long retaining a pro to provide personal protection

indicators.note: retaining means holding within, so the yearning word encloses the others

parts.note: to pine is to long for
taken as written
pro means in favour of, for

explanation.surface: An old bodyguard keeps a professional on hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pro' means in favour of, FOR, not a professional.
explanation.definitionFit: An apron-like garment worn to keep clothes clean.

clue.text: It just shows the heights to which one may rise!

definitions.text: It just shows the heights to which one may rise!

parts.words: It just shows the heights to which one may rise!
parts.note: reads like a proverb about ambition, but literally describes an instrument that displays how high an aircraft has climbed

explanation.surface: An encouraging remark about how far a person can go in life.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviation instrument indicates altitude, the height an aircraft has reached.

clue.text: A woman from a South American country

indicators.note: the name is taken out of the middle of a longer word in the clue, so this signals letters lifted from within

explanation.surface: Someone describes a lady who comes from Brazil or Peru.
explanation.walkthrough: The name sits inside the word 'American'; 'a South' and 'country' are only scenery.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, so it identifies a female person.

clue.text: Go astray and there'll be a charge made

parts.note: to err is to go wrong or wander from the right path
taken as written

explanation.surface: Wander off course and you will be billed for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' here is a task given to someone, not a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: A task entrusted to someone, such as a commission to fetch something, is a duty or mission.

clue.text: Colours, with article being read in two ways

indicators.note: the other pieces are placed within the two road abbreviations, read in between them

parts.note: ST is short for street, one kind of way
RD is short for road, a second kind of way
with means and, as in bread with butter
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Flags, plus a newspaper item that can be understood two different ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two ways' supplies both ST (street) and RD (road); 'being read in' puts AND plus A between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A regiment's colours are its flag, and a flag carried in battle is also called by this name.

clue.text: Mean, which is not in character

indicators.note: one word goes inside the other, as the clue says the negative word is placed in the letter

parts.note: a character is a letter of the alphabet; here the letter D spelt out as DEE
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is told they are unkind, which does not fit their nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' is a letter: D written out as its name, DEE, which takes NOT inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To signify or indicate something is what a word does when it means it.

clue.text: It's unknown for salesmen to be upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or disturbed, so the letters are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: Unnamed salesmen are annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Without a name, anonymous.

clue.text: Turned over only a quarter produced-so perverse

parts.note: S, south, is one of the four quarters of the compass

indicators.note: turned over means the word for only is flipped and read from end to start

parts.note: but means only, as in 'but a child'
born means brought into being, produced

explanation.surface: A person who flipped over just a quarter of the work and is being contrary about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned over' reverses BUT to TUB; the compass point S comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstinately refusing to change course is being contrary or wilful.

clue.text: Game, though that's of little significance

definitions.meaning: a table game with balls and pins

explanation.surface: A game which is unimportant.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar-billiards-style game and also a mere trifle, something unimportant.

clue.text: Noted speech

parts.note: noted suggests famous, but here means set to musical notes: the words of an opera

explanation.surface: A famous address.
explanation.definitionFit: The text of an opera, the words sung to music.

clue.text: Most dice are shaken in the private home

indicators.note: dice are shaken before a throw, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Most of the dice get rattled during a game played at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the household and family life rather than public affairs.

clue.text: Very large and very small figure in small department store

indicators.note: in puts the size and figure inside the department abbreviation

parts.note: DEPT is a short form of department
OS stands for outsize, very large
I is the figure one, a tiny number

explanation.surface: Sizes from huge to tiny on display in a little department store.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay down or put away for safekeeping, as in a bank.

clue.text: Way out English king with English craft

parts.note: E again abbreviates English
GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
E again abbreviates English
SS is a steamship, a sea craft

explanation.surface: An English king and an English vessel provide a means of escape.
explanation.walkthrough: GR is King George's royal cipher, seen on British postboxes.
explanation.definitionFit: An exit is the way you leave a place.

clue.text: Heartless fool with aim to get a decoration

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the word for fool is removed

parts.note: a sap is a fool
angle means aim, as in angling for something

explanation.surface: A foolish person aims to win a medal.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sparkling ornament sewn onto clothing.

clue.text: A swimmer has to cut back severely

indicators.note: back says the word for cut runs in the opposite direction

parts.note: to clip is to cut or trim
hard means severely, as in hit hard

explanation.surface: A swimmer is forced to make deep cutbacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses CLIP to PILC, followed by HARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A small oily sea fish, so a creature that swims.

clue.text: Sloth can be the ruination of a musician

indicators.note: the letters of the word are ruined and rebuilt into a name

explanation.surface: Laziness may destroy a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: Gustav Holst was an English composer, of The Planets.
explanation.definitionFit: An English composer, so a writer of music.

clue.text: Tart as can be making the beds

indicators.note: the letters of the two words can be made into something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A sharp-tongued person making up the beds in a house.
explanation.definitionFit: Layers of rock are called beds in geology.

clue.text: A friend will offer private backing within a very short time

indicators.note: within places the soldier inside the short time

parts.note: MO, a moment, is a very short time

indicators.note: backing means the word for private goes backwards

parts.note: GI is an American private soldier

explanation.surface: A pal will give a soldier support in a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns GI into IG, which sits inside MO.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish for a pal, used in English for a mate.

clue.text: Pilfer a pen?

definitions.meaning: to copy or steal another's work
a manger or stall for animals

explanation.surface: Steal a writing implement.
explanation.definitionFit: To copy dishonestly, and also a manger or animal stall.

clue.text: The head of state is a sovereign showing fibre

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: taken as written
a sovereign is a gold coin worth one pound, and L is the pound sign

explanation.surface: The head of state is a monarch who displays strength of character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fibre' looks like moral fibre in a ruler; a sovereign coin is worth a pound, abbreviated L.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong plant material from agave leaves, used for rope and twine.

clue.text: Exciting thing about running water

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for running water sits inside the word thing

parts.note: taken as written
a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: Something thrilling about a flowing stream.
explanation.definitionFit: Causing a rush of excitement or delight.

clue.text: Needing to adapt, but lose more in trying

indicators.note: the letters of the following words need to be adapted into a new order

explanation.surface: Something must change, but shedding more is hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Trying means difficult or tiresome, causing bother.
